text:
Contrast sensitivity of cats and humans in scotopic and mesopic conditions (synthetic fixture)

We measured contrast sensitivity of cats and humans with the same apparatus across scotopic and mesopic light levels.

At low spatial frequencies the cat's absolute threshold was 0.74 log units below the human threshold.

 Methods

Thresholds were measured behaviourally in a two-alternative forced-choice task with sinusoidal gratings at or below 1/8 cycle/deg.

Pupil area was measured in each session so that luminance could be converted to retinal illuminance.

 Results

Expressed in corneal luminance, the cat detected gratings at luminances 0.74 log units lower than the human observers did.

Expressed in retinal illuminance, after correcting for the larger pupil and ocular transmission, the cat's scotopic threshold was -0.08 log units re human.

 Discussion

Most of the cat's advantage is therefore optical: with optics factored out, scotopic sensitivity of cat and human is similar.
